title: Google VRP scope-strict, human-in-the-loop testing profile (design + guardrails, no live scanning yet)
goal: Design a controlled way for AegisPT to assist on Google's public Vulnerability Reward Program WITHOUT violating its rules: a hard scope-allowlist of in-scope Google domains, conservative rate limiting, no automated high-volume scanning, no DoS, no access to real user data, and a mandatory human-in-the-loop gate so the operator (a registered Google bug hunter) reviews and submits findings manually. Deliberately does NOT point the autonomous loop at Google production until AegisPT proves capability on the local labs.
scope: (1) Read and transcribe the live Google VRP rules + report process from bughunters.google.com (rules + /report) into a repo doc, including the exact wording that restricts automated scanning / request volume and the in-scope vs out-of-scope domain lists. (2) Specify a 'google-vrp' run profile: hard scope-allowlist (only in-scope Google domains, NO wildcard drift to non-Google hosts), strict per-host rate limit, request-volume cap, and a no-auto-submit gate. (3) Specify the human-in-the-loop reporting flow: agent proposes hypothesis + reproduction; operator validates and submits manually via /report. (4) Define a readiness precondition: this profile may only be exercised against Google after AegisPT autonomously solves >=1 lab-suite challenge (grader match=true) and the operator explicitly approves. Design/documentation only in this task.
generation_reason: Operator asked to read Google's VRP rules + report page and assess how AegisPT could test Google. Assessment: the program is authorized but its no-automated-scanning rule + DoS/real-user-data prohibitions + scope-drift legal risk make pointing the autonomous loop at Google production premature and rules-violating. Filed as a guardrails/design task to pursue safely later, after lab capability is proven.

constraints.active_task_gate: This package must be the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md before completion can be claimed.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Design + documentation + guardrail specification only. Do NOT run AegisPT against any Google production host in this task. No live scanning, no live exploitation, no submissions.
constraints.authorized_program_only: Any future live use is limited to Google's published in-scope VRP domains under their rules; never out-of-scope or third-party hosts.
constraints.no_automated_high_volume_scanning: The profile must enforce conservative rate limits and a request-volume cap consistent with Google's prohibition on automated scanning that degrades service.
constraints.human_in_the_loop_required: No autonomous submission. The operator (registered bug hunter) must validate and submit every finding manually.
constraints.readiness_precondition: Live use gated on >=1 autonomous lab-suite solve (grader match=true) AND explicit operator approval.

success_criteria: Doc: repo file transcribes the live VRP rules + report process, with the exact automated-scanning / volume restriction wording quoted and the in-scope vs out-of-scope domain lists captured.
Spec: a 'google-vrp' run profile is specified with a hard in-scope-domain allowlist, per-host rate limit, request-volume cap, and no-auto-submit gate.
Spec: the human-in-the-loop reporting flow is documented end to end.
Gate: the readiness precondition (>=1 autonomous lab solve + operator approval) is written into the profile and cannot be bypassed.
No live Google traffic is generated by this task.
must_not_touch: api/app/services/assessment_loop.py picker behavior (no live-scan wiring in this task)
workers/runners/ network behavior against external hosts
Capability pack registry / validation / approval / runtime binding flows

acceptance_criteria: Doc records the exact VRP wording on automated scanning + volume and the in-scope/out-of-scope domain lists.
Profile spec enforces scope-allowlist, rate limit, volume cap, and no-auto-submit.
Readiness precondition and human-in-the-loop gate are explicit and unbypassable.
No live Google requests were made during the task.
